meta.prestige_main: Tier B leakage-free: log1p(max prior papers of first/last author) + max years active

measurement.snapshot_statement: Upvotes are cumulative HF counts at scrape time (2026-06-05 for 2024–25 papers, 2026-06-11 for 2023 papers), not day-one counts; citations are Semantic Scholar counts at the 2026-06-11 snapshot; age_months = months from the HF published_at date to 2026-06-11 (5.4–39.8).

M6_plus_text.label: M6 + text/format controls (authors, title, abstract, GitHub, kw flags)

M4_legacy_subfield_taxonomy.note: legacy 26-level `subfield` (two taxonomies keyed on upvotes) instead of subfield_kw

M4_no_log_age.note: month FE only, no within-month log-age term

M4_plus_appear_prior.note: + log1p prior-only author HF appearances (v1 'recurrence prestige', look-ahead removed)

M4_plus_appear_LOOKAHEAD.note: + log1p author_max_appear as stored (48% look-ahead) — shown only to quantify the leak

M4_plus_comments.note: + log1p HF comments (second attention signal, cumulative at scrape)

M4_upvote_rank_in_month.note: treatment = within-release-month percentile rank of upvotes (0..1); beta = bottom-to-top gap

M4_ai_keywords_only_labels.note: papers whose subfield_kw came from ai_keywords (drop title/summary fallback + Other)

ladder_convexity.note: M4 + log_upvotes^2. Positive squared term = elasticity rises with attention; Poisson-QMLE weights papers by their expected count, so it is dominated by the top tail and returns a larger average IRR than NB2 (which down-weights high counts) or log-OLS (geometric mean).

bootstrap_M4.note: block bootstrap over release months (34 clusters), percentile 95% CI; each rep refits M4

e_value_M4.note: VanderWeele–Ding E-value on the risk-ratio scale (IRR per doubling of upvotes). Minimum strength of association an unmeasured confounder needs with BOTH attention and citations to explain the estimate away. Not a causal claim — a sensitivity summary.

placebo_permutation_M4.note: log_upvotes permuted within release_month × subfield_kw cells; M4 refit each time
placebo_permutation_M4.additive_fe_note: With additive month + subfield FE the placebo mean is slightly positive because permuting within month × subfield cells preserves cell-mean upvotes, and cell means of upvotes and citations co-move beyond the additive FE. The cell-FE variant below (release_month × subfield_kw interacted FE) removes this and is centred at ~0.

placebo_outcome_reference_count_M4.note: reference count is fixed at submission; attention should not 'predict' it if controls are adequate. n excludes 771 papers with reference_count = 0 (S2 parse gaps).

hierarchical_mixedlm.spec: log_citations ~ log_upvotes + log_age + tierB_prior + tierB_yrs + tierB_miss + C(release_month) + C(dow)  | groups = subfield_kw, re_formula = ~log_upvotes (REML)
hierarchical_mixedlm.why_not_poisson_glmm: statsmodels has no maximum-likelihood Poisson/NB GLMM with correlated random intercept+slope and cluster-robust SEs (only a variational-Bayes PoissonBayesMixedGLM); the count-scale association is therefore estimated with FE Poisson/NB (ladder) and the hierarchical/heterogeneity part with this linear mixed model on log1p citations, as in the June-11 analysis but with the uniform taxonomy and month FE.

lr_test_random_slope.note: ML fits; 50:50 chi2(1)/chi2(2) mixture for the boundary

dose_response_deciles.note: deciles of raw upvotes (ties split by order); adjusted = residual of log1p cites on log age + subfield_kw + month FE, plus grand mean

design.ps_model: logit(treat) ~ Tier B prior papers (log1p) + years active + Tier B-missing flag + log age + subfield_kw dummies + release_month dummies
design.matching: 1:1 nearest neighbour on logit(PS), with replacement, caliper 0.2 SD of logit(PS)
design.ipw: ATT weights ps/(1-ps) for controls, stabilised by P(T=0)/P(T=1), trimmed at the 99th pct, normalised (Hajek)
design.cem: exact cells release_month × subfield_kw × Tier B prior-papers quintile (missing = own bin)
design.bootstrap: 300 paper-level reps stratified by treatment; PS refit + rematch each rep

variant_ps_with_hindex_LEAKY.note: PS also includes log1p max/last author h-index measured 2026-06-11 (as the June-11 v2 analysis did). h-index is downstream of citations, so this over-adjusts; shown to explain the gap to v2's 1.15 / 0.75.

over_under.definition: attention residual = log1p upvotes minus OLS fit on log age + subfield_kw FE + release_month FE; impact residual = same for log1p citations; percentile ranks over all 11,344 papers. overrated = attention pct >= 2/3 AND impact pct <= 1/3; underrated = attention pct <= 1/3 AND impact pct >= 2/3; else neutral.

overrated_vs_rest.note: statsmodels Logit, cluster-robust by release_month; continuous features standardised (OR per SD); h-index features are 2026-measured (LEAKY, Matthew effect on the outcome side)

underrated_vs_rest.note: statsmodels Logit, cluster-robust by release_month; continuous features standardised (OR per SD); h-index features are 2026-measured (LEAKY, Matthew effect on the outcome side)

overrated_vs_underrated.note: statsmodels Logit, cluster-robust by release_month; continuous features standardised (OR per SD); h-index features are 2026-measured (LEAKY, Matthew effect on the outcome side)

overrated_vs_rest_NOLEAK.note: statsmodels Logit, cluster-robust by release_month; continuous features standardised (OR per SD); h-index features EXCLUDED (leakage-free driver model)

underrated_vs_rest_NOLEAK.note: statsmodels Logit, cluster-robust by release_month; continuous features standardised (OR per SD); h-index features EXCLUDED (leakage-free driver model)

overrated_vs_underrated_NOLEAK.note: statsmodels Logit, cluster-robust by release_month; continuous features standardised (OR per SD); h-index features EXCLUDED (leakage-free driver model)

max_prior_papers_true_w99.label: Tier B max prior papers of first/last author (w99, leakage-free)

max_years_active.label: Tier B max years active before the paper

title_themes.note: TF-IDF (1-2 grams, min_df 5, english stop words) on TITLES only; L1 logistic overrated(1) vs underrated(0), balanced; 5-fold CV AUC reported as the (weak) separability of the two groups by title alone

title_keyword_themes_secondary.note: same model on title + HF ai_keywords (secondary)

over_under.examples_note: chosen by largest |attention pct - impact pct| among papers with age >= 12 months AND citation_count >= 1; zero-citation records at >= 12 months are excluded because several are Semantic Scholar matching failures (e.g. 2410.05258 'Differential Transformer', 182 upvotes, 0 recorded citations) rather than genuinely uncited papers.

overrated_zero_citation_records.note: some of these are S2 match failures, i.e. part of the 'over-rated' set is measurement error on the impact side

When Less is Enough: Adaptive Token Reduction for Efficient Image Representation
VS-Bench: Evaluating VLMs for Strategic Reasoning and Decision-Making in Multi-Agent Environments

underrated.title: TraceVLA: Visual Trace Prompting Enhances Spatial-Temporal Awareness for Generalist Robotic Policies

control_sample_facts.construction: Project/scripts/10: for each month × stratum {cs.CL, cs.CV, cs.LG} the first ~40 arXiv submissions by submittedDate ascending (i.e. the first day(s) of the month), de-duplicated across strata, minus ids that ever trended on HF; S2 citations/h-index fetched 2026-06-11.
control_sample_facts.control_subfield_note: Controls have no ai_keywords/abstract text, only titles: the SAME 13-level keyword rule set was applied to titles (labels ~53%); the remainder is mapped from the arXiv primary category to the nearest keyword label (cs.CV/eess.IV -> Vision-Perception, cs.CL/cs.LG/stat.ML/cs.AI -> LLM-core, cs.RO -> Robotics/Embodied, cs.SD/eess.AS -> Speech/Audio, cs.IR -> RAG/Retrieval, cs.SE -> Code/Math, else Other). On trending papers the title-only rule agrees with subfield_kw for ~64% of the labelled ones, so the subfield match is coarse; a 4-family variant is also reported.

bottom_tertile_attention_residual.desc: trending papers in the bottom tertile of the age/field/month-adjusted attention residual, regardless of citations [honest]

bottom_tertile_raw_upvotes.desc: trending papers with upvotes <= 9 (bottom tertile of raw upvotes), regardless of citations

top_tertile_attention_residual.desc: trending papers in the top tertile of the adjusted attention residual (context)

underrated_label_OUTCOME_SELECTED.desc: v2-style 'under-rated' = bottom-tertile attention AND top-tertile citation residual — selected on the outcome; shown only to document why the 91st-percentile claim was circular
